properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] SSRF-Driven Secret Egress: Public-Facing App Reaches Cloud Metadata/Attacker Host
properties.description:
Detects an unauthenticated public-facing application that, shortly after receiving an inbound request, makes a server-side outbound connection to the cloud instance-metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / fd00:ec2::254) or an attacker-named callback host — the tell-tale of a server-side request forgery being used to steal secrets. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of maximum-severity advisories all share this exact primitive: OpenDJ's DSMLv2 gateway dereferences attacker-supplied xsd:anyURI values (GHSA-68r5-9hpg-7qw9), Flyto2 Core's unauthenticated /run reflects callback_url and attaches X-Internal-Key: $FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET (CVE-2026-67426), and Budibase forwards stored REST-datasource credentials to any host a query names (GHSA-mqhr-6j6h-74p5) — with OpenAM (CVE-2026-62379) and Ruflo MCP (CVE-2026-59726) providing the unauthenticated RCE that reaches the same egress. It spans the exploit (T1190) → credential-access (IMDS/secret read) → exfiltration (secret leaves over the app's own socket) kill-chain stages. It FIRES when a server runtime (java, node, ruby, python, w3wp, nginx) egresses to a metadata IP or listed C2 host within the correlation window of an inbound public request, and when EC2 instance-role credentials appear off-instance; it does NOT fire on normal user browsing, on SDK-driven IMDS calls that never follow an inbound public request, or on internal-only service-to-service traffic.

Rationale: Every article in scope terminates in the same behaviour — an unauthenticated public-facing app is coerced into making a server-side outbound request that carries a secret (IMDS role creds, runner secret, or stored datasource token) — so keying on server-runtime egress-to-metadata/attacker-host correlated with a preceding inbound request catches the shared primitive rather than any one CVE's IOCs.
